Implemented the fix in django/db/models/sql/query.py.

Change: In `get_aggregation`, added a `has_window` detection that checks whether any annotation contains a window function (`contains_over_clause`), and included it in the condition that decides whether to wrap the query in an inner subquery. When window functions are present, the aggregation is now computed in an outer query over an inner subquery that computes the window function, avoiding the PostgreSQL error "aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls".

Verification: Ran the public regression selection (`aggregation`), which passed — 124 tests, OK, returncode 0. Note that public regression success does not guarantee host feature acceptance, which is run separately by the host.
